Pursuant to California Government Code Section 65912.160(e), the City Council adopts this ordinance on eligible sites meeting one of the criteria referenced below, making the sites permanently exempt from Senate Bill 79, codified at Government Code, Title 7, Division 1, Chapter 4.1.5 (Senate Bill 79):
locate_in_source: Located in ordinance-188968 (8 pages, City OCR text layer): Section 1 and its criteria A and B, page 4; Sec. 3 (maps), page 5; Sec. 6 (ZIMAS), page 6; recitals on the SCAG final map, page 3.
question_for_human_reviewer: Ordinance 188968 Section 1 makes sites meeting either criterion (no walking path under one mile to the TOD stop, or an industrial employment hub) permanently exempt from SB 79, and Section 3 delegates the exemption maps to the Director of Planning. Do you agree that a permanent exemption shown on the Director's map is a disqualifier for the SB 79 pathway, that 'none shown' must stay requires_judgment until the SCAG final map exists, and that the fact should be renamed from 'exclusion' to 'exemption' with its category? Should the ZIMAS display that Section 6 directs remain observation-only?

proposed_controlled_interpretation.controlled_values_required: Rename sb79-permanent-exclusion to sb79-permanent-exemption with controlled values walking_path (Sec. 1.A) | industrial_employment_hub (Sec. 1.B) | none_shown | not_retrieved, human-recorded from the Director's exemption map with its publication date.
proposed_controlled_interpretation.narrowing_note: Replace the yes/no with the category from the Director's map. The ordinance says 'permanently exempt'.
proposed_controlled_interpretation.predicate_shape_if_reviewer_agrees: walking_path or industrial_employment_hub -> disqualifying_per_source; none_shown -> requires_judgment while the SCAG final map is pending; not_retrieved -> unknown.
must_remain_unresolved_when: the Director's exemption map was not retrieved or is undated
the map shows no exemption while the SCAG final TOD map is not produced
the ZIMAS display and the Director's map disagree
proposed_controlled_interpretation.zimas_conflict_risk: High. Sec. 6 directs the Director to show in ZIMAS which sites are and are not covered by SB 79, so ZIMAS may carry the most current display, but it is neither the ordinance nor the Director's map. zimas-sb79-exemption does not distinguish permanent from temporary exemption and stays observation-only; any divergence raises program_flag_divergence.

excerpts.text: Section 1. Pursuant to California Government Code Section 65912.160(e), the City Council adopts this ordinance on eligible sites meeting one of the criteria referenced below, making the sites permanently exempt from Senate Bill 79, codified at Government Code, Title 7, Division 1, Chapter 4.1.5 (Senate Bill 79):

candidate_components.controlled_value_encoding: Both categories have the same effect; the category is recorded for traceability.
candidate_components.proposed_rule_if_reviewer_agrees: walking_path or industrial_employment_hub -> disqualifying_per_source for the SB 79 pathway. none_shown -> requires_judgment while the SCAG final map is pending. not_retrieved -> unknown.
judgment_or_ambiguity: The ordinance lists no parcels; whether a site meets a criterion is a mapping determination (Sec. 3), so absence from a provisional map is not a finding.
The repository calls this an 'exclusion'; the ordinance says 'permanently exempt'.

candidate_components.label: Criterion A: no walking path of less than one mile to the TOD stop

excerpts.text: A. A site for which there exists no walking path of less than one mile from that location to the transit-oriented development stop (Gov. Code Sec. 65912.160(e)(1));

candidate_components.controlled_value_encoding: None; rely on the Director's map.
judgment_or_ambiguity: Needs a walking-network analysis to SCAG-designated TOD stops, which are not final.

candidate_components.label: Criterion B: industrial employment hub

excerpts.text: B. A site designated as an industrial employment hub if the City has at least 15 transit-oriented development stops.

candidate_components.controlled_value_encoding: None; rely on the Director's map.
judgment_or_ambiguity: Needs the General Plan employment-lands designation made on or before January 1, 2025, a 250-acre contiguity test, and the industrial-use test of GCS 65912.121.

candidate_components.label: Which record shows a parcel's exemption
candidate_components.pinpoint: Ordinance 188968, Sec. 3, page 5; Sec. 6, page 6; recital, page 3

excerpts.text: By enacting this ordinance, the City Council grants the Director of Planning with the power and duty, consistent with City Charter Section 553, to issue and update maps with eligible transit-oriented development sites meeting the criteria for permanent or temporarily exempt status

(1) indicate on its public facing zoning map in the Zone Information and Map Access System (ZIMAS), which sites or transit-oriented development zones are and are not covered by Senate Bill 79’s provisions;

WHEREAS, eligibility for the Phased Implementation Ordinance is contingent on the availability of a final map which has not yet been produced and approved by the Southern California Association of Governments

candidate_components.controlled_value_encoding: A design decision for the reviewer, not a fact.
judgment_or_ambiguity: Sec. 6 directs the City to show SB 79 coverage in ZIMAS. Making ZIMAS the record would be a design change, not a verification.
The recital says the SCAG final map is not produced, so eligibility rests on current data and can change.
